skill.name: web-accessibility

content.user_title: Audit Web Accessibility for WCAG Compliance
content.value_statement: Accessibility gaps can block users and create compliance risk. This skill guides WCAG audits, screen reader checks, keyboard testing, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Assess WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 conformance levels for web pages.
Review semantic HTML, headings, landmarks, and ARIA usage.
Check keyboard navigation paths, focus order, and focus visibility.
Identify color contrast issues against Level AA and AAA targets.
Evaluate image text alternatives, form labels, and error messaging.
Produce prioritized accessibility fixes with clear user impact.
limitations: Does not run automated browser tests unless the host agent provides tools.
Cannot verify screen reader output without access to assistive technology.
Requires page source, screenshots, or a live site for precise findings.
WCAG interpretations may need legal or organizational review for formal compliance.

use_cases.title: Audit a Release Candidate
use_cases.description: Review key pages before launch and list WCAG issues by severity and user impact.

use_cases.title: Improve Inclusive Interaction Design
use_cases.description: Check focus states, keyboard flows, labels, and contrast before design handoff.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Create a structured issue summary for accessibility tracking and stakeholder review.

prompt_templates.title: Quick WCAG Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page for WCAG 2.2 Level AA issues. Focus on headings, links, images, forms, and color contrast.

prompt_templates.title: Keyboard Navigation Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this flow for keyboard accessibility. Check tab order, focus visibility, skip links, traps, and operable controls.

prompt_templates.title: Component Remediation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this component for accessibility issues. Provide prioritized fixes for semantics, ARIA, focus management, and error messaging.

prompt_templates.title: Full Release Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a WCAG 2.2 audit for these screens. Group findings by severity, criterion, affected users, and recommended remediation.

output_examples.input: Audit a product homepage for WCAG Level AA.
output: Critical: The hero image needs meaningful alternative text.
High: The newsletter field needs a visible label and clear error text.
Medium: Button text contrast should be increased to meet Level AA.

output_examples.input: Review keyboard navigation for a checkout flow.
output: The focus order should follow the visual order from cart summary to payment.
The modal needs a reliable escape path and focus return behavior.
Disabled controls need clear status text for keyboard and screen reader users.

output_examples.input: Improve accessibility for a form component.
output: Add persistent labels for every input.
Connect errors to the related fields in the accessibility tree.
Use clear instructions before validation, not only after failure.

best_practices: Provide the page URL, affected components, and target WCAG level before requesting an audit.
Include screenshots or source snippets when visual contrast or semantic structure matters.
Validate recommendations with keyboard testing and assistive technology when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on automated scores for accessibility approval.
Do not add ARIA when native HTML already provides the correct semantics.
Do not treat color alone as the only way to communicate state or errors.

faq.question: Which WCAG versions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on WCAG 2.1 and 2.2, including Level A, AA, and AAA considerations.

faq.question: Can it replace a full accessibility audit?
faq.answer: No. It supports review and remediation, but formal audits may require specialist testing and organizational signoff.

faq.question: Does it test with real screen readers?
faq.answer: Only when the host environment provides access. Otherwise, it reviews semantics and expected screen reader behavior.

faq.question: Can it review designs before code exists?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review labels, contrast, focus expectations, content structure, and interaction requirements from design materials.

faq.question: What inputs improve the results?
faq.answer: Provide URLs, screenshots, HTML snippets, component names, user flows, and the required WCAG conformance level.

faq.question: Does it provide remediation guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains accessibility issues and suggests practical fixes with priority and user impact.
